lessons.title: The big two and the chasers
lessons.objective: You can explain El Clásico and why Atlético is the usual third party.

options.text: The match between Real Madrid and Barcelona in La Liga

explanation.correct: Right. El Clásico is the name for matches between Real Madrid and Barcelona, two of the biggest clubs in the world.
explanation.incorrect: El Clásico is the fixture between Real Madrid and Barcelona, La Liga's two dominant clubs.
explanation.sayThisLine: When's the Clásico, that's the one everyone watches.

payload.prompt: Why is Atlético Madrid usually the third-best team in La Liga?

options.text: They play in a smaller stadium
Real Madrid and Barcelona's size, budgets and history make it hard for anyone else to match them
They have a rule against signing big-name players

explanation.correct: Right. Real Madrid and Barcelona are among the biggest clubs in the world, which gives them an edge in signing and keeping the best players.
explanation.incorrect: Real Madrid and Barcelona's size and winning traditions leave Atlético fighting hard for third, even when they are well run and dangerous.
explanation.sayThisLine: Atletico always punches above their weight, but Clásico clubs have the money.

statement.speaker: A Spanish fan
statement.text: Clásico weekend is basically a holiday.

options.text: El Clásico matches are hugely important and draw massive attention in Spain
The teams take Clásico weekend off and do not play other matches
There is no real rivalry between the clubs

payload.translation: El Clásico is so important in Spain that the whole country stops to watch. The passion and history make it feel like more than just a game.

followUps.line: What kind of rivalry exists between them?
followUps.why: You're curious about the history, not just the result.

followUps.line: Has one team dominated the other in recent years?
followUps.why: A real follow-up that builds on what they said.

followUps.line: Where do your friends or family stand on this one?
followUps.why: You're connecting their passion to people you know.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You don't need to have a take; real fans just name what they saw.

payload.prompt: Match these Spanish clubs to their roles.

pairs.definition: Spanish giant with 15 European Cups, a La Liga heavyweight
Spanish powerhouse known for tiki-taka and European glory
Challenger, usually third in La Liga, known for grit

distractorDefinitions: A team in the Spanish second division
A La Liga team based in the Basque region

explanation.summary: These three clubs define La Liga. Real Madrid and Barcelona are the giants; Atlético is the competitor with character.

explanation.correct: Right. Real Madrid and Barcelona are Spain's biggest clubs, and their rivalry is one of sport's greatest.
explanation.incorrect: El Clásico is the name for Real Madrid versus Barcelona, the two clubs that have dominated La Liga for decades.

exchanges.theirMessage: Did you watch the Clásico? It was electric.

replies.theirResponse: Honestly, the momentum swung about four times in the second half. Nobody could relax.

exchanges.theirMessage: The way they're passing around is so clean, reminds me of the old Barça.

replies.text: That's that Spanish style right? The possession thing?
replies.theirResponse: Exactly, they're all about keeping the ball and moving into space.
replies.coachNote: Curious question about style—you're showing you want to understand what they see.

replies.text: Yeah, Barcelona was unbeatable with that.
replies.theirResponse: They really were at their peak.
replies.coachNote: True but pretty surface-level. What specifically impressed you about how they're moving?

lessons.title: Spanish style
lessons.objective: You can explain how Spanish teams think about possession.

payload.prompt: What is the idea behind positional play in Spanish football?

options.text: Kick the ball as far as possible and run to it
Players occupy zones so the ball carrier always has passing options nearby
Only the striker is allowed to move forward

explanation.correct: Right. Spanish teams create a web of passing angles by putting players in zones where they support each other, not by playing it long.
explanation.incorrect: Positional play is about placing players so they form a connected network of passes. It's not about distance, it's about angles and support.
explanation.sayThisLine: It's positional play, not just passing for passing's sake.

payload.prompt: What do Barcelona and Spain achieve with tiki-taka?

options.text: They wear down opponents by keeping the ball and creating chances through patience and triangles
They confuse the referee by passing the ball quickly
They save time by avoiding tackles

explanation.correct: Right. Tiki-taka is about keeping the ball with short passes and triangles, controlling the game and waiting for openings instead of rushing.
explanation.incorrect: Tiki-taka uses short passing and movement into space to control the game. By keeping the ball, they tire opponents and create gaps.
explanation.sayThisLine: It's tiki-taka, endless passing until the gap opens.

statement.speaker: Tactical analyst
statement.text: It's not passing for passing's sake, it's positional play.

options.text: Spanish teams pass a lot but with a purpose: to create spaces and angles
They pass the ball to avoid playing real football
Every pass has to go further up the pitch

payload.translation: Spanish football looks pretty because every pass sets up the next player. It's not just about quantity of passes; it's about quality of position.

followUps.line: Have you noticed how the Spanish style uses the width of the pitch differently?
followUps.why: You're spotting the tactical pattern they're describing.

followUps.line: Do you prefer watching that style or a more direct approach?
followUps.why: A honest take on what you enjoy, not fake expertise.

followUps.line: Who else plays positional play besides the Spanish?
followUps.why: You're curious about how the style spreads beyond Spain.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You can say what you noticed without being an analyst.

payload.prompt: Match Spanish football concepts to their meanings.

pairs.definition: Short-passing style built on triangles and patient movement
Players occupy zones so the ball carrier always has options

explanation.summary: Spanish football is built on positioning and possession. Tiki-taka is the beautiful way Barcelona made it famous worldwide.

explanation.correct: Right. Spanish football combines tiki-taka (short-passing possession) with positional play (occupying zones). It's built on control and patience.
explanation.incorrect: Spanish style is built on tiki-taka (short passes in triangles) and positional play (players occupying zones), creating control and chances.

exchanges.theirMessage: I love how Barcelona builds from the back. Zero rush.

replies.text: How does the slow build help them?
replies.theirResponse: It tires opponents out and pulls them out of shape. By the time they attack, there's space everywhere.
replies.coachNote: Great question—you're curious about the why behind the style, not just the what.

replies.text: Yeah, they're so good at passing.
replies.coachNote: True but basic. What do you notice about where the players move into after the pass?

replies.text: That's boring, teams should just shoot.
replies.theirResponse: I guess we watch for different things.
replies.coachNote: You dismissed what they like. Even if you prefer direct play, you can ask why they love the style.

exchanges.theirMessage: The way they move into space after passing is incredible. That's positional play.

replies.text: So is it like always having a triangle around the ball?
replies.theirResponse: Exactly. Always three options, always a way out. You get the idea.
replies.coachNote: You spotted the pattern they're describing and asked a sharp follow-up.

replies.text: That's why they're so hard to beat.
replies.coachNote: True, but you could dig deeper—what happens if a team presses them high?

replies.text: I don't see what's special about running around.
replies.theirResponse: You're not really watching the positioning.
replies.coachNote: Dismissing what they value makes them feel like you're not listening.
